sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: Front matter of the Spanish edition of the WHO guideline on digital interventions for health system strengthening, beginning with the title page. It includes the 2022 copyright and cataloguing page with ISBNs, Creative Commons licence terms and standard disclaimers. A table of contents follows, listing the chapters, annexes on contributors, declarations of interest and evidence maps, and English-only web supplements with GRADE tables and evidence-to-decision frameworks.

sections.title: Prólogo

summary.text: The foreword by the WHO Director-General, which places digital technologies in the long history of health advances and gives examples such as rapid diagnostics, 3-D printing, telemedicine and artificial intelligence. It presents the guideline as evidence to help countries invest wisely and stresses that digital tools are means to promote health and serve the vulnerable, not ends in themselves.

sections.extract: A lo largo de la historia, la salud de los seres humanos ha mejorado gracias a los avances en la tecnología. Desde el desarrollo del saneamiento moderno hasta la aparición de la penicilina, la anestesia, las vacunas y las imágenes por resonancia magnética, todos estos avances en la salud siempre dependieron de la ciencia, la investigación y la tecnología, sus propulsores clave. No hay diferencias en la actualidad.

summary.text: The acknowledgements, naming the WHO Department of Reproductive Health and Research staff who coordinated the guideline, the Norwegian Institute of Public Health team that gave methodological support, and the many WHO staff and regional advisers involved. It also credits the designers and lists the funders, stating that they did not influence the content.

sections.extract: La Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS) quiere agradecer a todas las personas y las organizaciones que contribuyeron durante muchos años a la elaboración de esta directriz. sections.title: Resumen ejecutivo

summary.text: The executive summary of the guideline, which defines eHealth, mHealth and digital health and recalls the 2018 World Health Assembly resolution asking WHO for normative guidance on evidence-based digital interventions. It warns that enthusiasm has led to many short-lived implementations with little evaluation of benefits and harms. Using an adapted Tanahashi model, it explains how health system shortfalls limit universal health coverage and how digital interventions might address them. It ends with a figure linking ten recommendations, on birth and death notification, stock notification, telemedicine, targeted client communication, decision support, digital tracking and training, to the health system challenges they address.

sections.title: Objetivos de esta directriz

summary.text: States that the guideline responds to the 2018 World Health Assembly resolution on digital health and aims to give recommendations based on critical appraisal of evidence on benefits, harms, acceptability, feasibility, resource use and equity. It lists the digital interventions covered, including birth and death notification, stock management, telemedicine, targeted client communication, decision support, digital tracking and health worker training.

sections.title: Público destinatario

summary.text: Identifies the main audience as health ministry decision-makers and public health professionals, as well as implementing and development partners, and notes that the recommended interventions, though reviewed for mobile devices, can be used on any digital device.

sections.title: Vínculos con otros recursos de la OMS

summary.text: Explains that WHO had not previously issued normative guidance specifically on digital health interventions, and lists WHO clinical guidelines that already include digital elements, such as those on HIV, TB and community health workers. It also describes related WHO resources, including the classification of digital health interventions, the Digital Health Atlas and the Be He@lthy, Be Mobile initiative with ITU.

sections.title: Contexto y entorno propicio

summary.text: Describes how the maturity of the enabling environment and ICT environment, including leadership, governance, policy, financing, workforce, standards and interoperability, affects the impact of digital interventions. It cautions that adopting the recommendations must not undermine quality care where digital tools are unavailable or unaccepted, and that weak ecosystems should first be strengthened.

summary.text: Stresses that digital interventions should fit into a coherent digital health architecture rather than operate as isolated duplicates. It points to complementary resources such as the WHO/ITU National eHealth Strategy Toolkit and the ITU Digital Health Platform Handbook, and lists communities of practice including the African Alliance, AeHIN and OpenHIE.

sections.title: Enfoque de directrices activas

summary.text: Describes the living guideline approach, under which this first version covers a priority list of mobile-accessible digital interventions and later versions will add further interventions and health areas as evidence emerges. It gives the example of extending targeted client communication to noncommunicable diseases.

sections.extract: Enfoque de directrices activas Esta directriz incluye recomendaciones sobre una lista de intervenciones de salud digital prioritarias a las que se puede tener acceso mediante dispositivos móviles, que son un subconjunto de una serie mucho más amplia de intervenciones digitales. La directriz prevé incorporar de forma gradual un conjunto más vasto de intervenciones de salud digital emergentes en versiones posteriores.

sections.title: Métodos

summary.text: Summarizes the methods used, following the WHO handbook for guideline development, with two online surveys and three meetings held in February 2016, September 2016 and June 2018 to set the scope, prioritize questions and formulate recommendations.

sections.extract: En la elaboración de esta directriz, se siguieron los métodos descritos en la segunda edición del WHO handbook for guideline development (Manual de la OMS para la elaboración de directrices) (35). sections.title: Identificación de las preguntas prioritarias

summary.text: Describes how priority questions were identified, starting from the WHO classification of digital health interventions and its list of health system challenges, and drafted in PICO format. It explains that questions were refined at a virtual consultation and scoping meeting and ranked through two surveys of more than 300 respondents from all WHO regions.

sections.title: Delimitación del alcance de las intervenciones y los resultados

summary.text: Lists the nine digital health interventions prioritized for evidence review, from birth and death notification to telemedicine, targeted client communication, decision support, digital tracking and health worker training. Table 2.1 defines each intervention with synonyms, and the text describes the outcomes considered. It notes that the reviews focused on mobile access for low-resource settings without excluding other devices. No restrictions were placed on delivery channels such as voice, text messages or interactive voice response.

sections.title: Recuperación de la evidencia

summary.text: Explains the two types of evidence considered: effectiveness evidence from randomized trials and other controlled studies, and qualitative evidence on acceptability, feasibility and implementation. It notes that cost evidence came only from included studies and programme documents, and describes an overarching analysis of cross-cutting factors from qualitative reviews and other syntheses.

sections.extract: Se consideraron dos tipos de evidencias para esta directriz: Ⱥ evidencia de la eficacia de las intervenciones de salud digital basados en ensayos clínicos aleatorizados (ECA), estudios no aleatorios, estudios controlados de tipo antes y después y estudios de series temporales interrumpidas (STI); y Ⱥ evidencia de los factores que influyen en la aceptabilidad, la factibilidad y la implementación de las intervenciones

summary.text: Describes how risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane and EPOC criteria for effectiveness studies and a critical appraisal tool for qualitative studies. It explains how certainty of effectiveness evidence was graded and how confidence in qualitative findings was rated with the CERQual approach as high, moderate, low or very low.

summary.text: Explains that the recommendations appear in the executive summary, with evidence summaries in Chapter 3, and that relevant existing WHO recommendations are quoted exactly with contextual remarks.

sections.extract: Las recomendaciones se presentan en el resumen ejecutivo de esta directriz. Para cada recomendación, en el Capítulo 3 se presenta un resumen de la evidencia acerca de los efectos positivos y negativos de la intervención, su aceptación y factibilidad, su repercusión en la equidad y en los derechos de género y humanos, el uso de recursos y cualquier otra consideración analizada en la reunión del grupo de elaboración

sections.title: Evidencia y recomendaciones

summary.text: Introduces the chapter of evidence-based recommendations, which this Spanish text numbers as nine, on prioritised digital health interventions. It lists what is given for each intervention and points to annexes and web supplements for evidence gaps and evidence-to-decision frameworks.

sections.extract: recomendaciones En esta directriz se presentan nueve recomendaciones basadas en la evidencia sobre las intervenciones de salud digital que se priorizaron durante el proceso de delimitación del alcance (véanse las secciones 2.1 y 2.2). Estas recomendaciones se realizan con la expectativa de que su implementación dependa del conocimiento de la madurez y la preparación del ecosistema, como se describe en el Capítulo 4.

sections.title: Hallazgos transversales de aceptabilidad y factibilidad

summary.text: Summarises cross-cutting qualitative findings on the acceptability and feasibility of digital interventions used by health workers, based on evidence syntheses. It covers factors that may raise or lower acceptability for health workers and practical feasibility issues. Findings on clients and their concerns are also included. The end of the block begins the section on birth and death notification and its links to civil registration.

sections.extract: aceptabilidad y factibilidad La mayoría de las intervenciones de salud digital de esta directriz están centradas en los trabajadores sanitarios o previstas para que ellos las utilicen. Los siguientes hallazgos apuntan a factores que influyen en la aceptabilidad y factibilidad de las intervenciones digitales que utilizan los trabajadores sanitarios. sections.title: Cobertura de recuentos: notificación de nacimientos y defunciones

summary.text: Covers digital birth and death notification, listing health system challenges such as missing population denominators and delays in reporting events. It notes that wider access to mobile devices among community actors can extend civil registration coverage and summarises the evidence. WHO recommends digital birth notification where it gives individual-level data to a system able to respond, and digital death notification only in the context of rigorous research under similar conditions. Implementation considerations include linking birth notification to high-coverage services such as immunisation while checking that registration systems can absorb more notifications.

sections.title: Disponibilidad de productos básicos: notificación de stock y productos básicos

summary.text: Covers digital stock notification and commodity management, explaining the importance of commodity availability for quality care and universal health coverage and the problem of stock-outs. It summarises the evidence and implementation issues. WHO recommends the intervention where supply chain systems can respond promptly and appropriately to notifications, despite limited evidence of effectiveness. The block ends by introducing telemedicine as a way to improve access to health facilities and staff.

summary.text: Covers digital decision support for health workers, addressing poor guideline adherence, inadequate referrals and limited competence. It notes that decision support tools are well established and increasingly delivered on mobile devices, and summarises the evidence. WHO recommends decision support for tasks already within health workers' defined scope of practice. The block ends by introducing digital tracking of clients' health status and services.

sections.title: Consideraciones sobre la implementación

summary.text: Notes that digital health shares underlying problems of other health system interventions, such as weak management, poor training and infrastructure limits, so context and the enabling environment are crucial.

sections.extract: la implementación La salud digital puede ayudar a resolver problemas como la distancia y el acceso, pero, aun así, comparte muchos de los desafíos subyacentes que enfrentan las intervenciones del sistema sanitario en general, entre ellos, deficiencias en la gestión, capacitación insuficiente, limitaciones infraestructurales y poco acceso a los equipos y los suministros. sections.title: Cómo vincular las recomendaciones en el sistema sanitario

summary.text: Explains how the different digital health recommendations meet health system needs in connected ways, from commodity availability for managers to access to information and services for clients. A figure shows how notification, telemedicine, targeted communication, decision support and mobile learning together support accountable, high-quality care.

sections.extract: en el sistema sanitario Si bien las recomendaciones incluidas en esta directriz se basan en distintas intervenciones digitales, todas colaboran a satisfacer las necesidades de los sistemas sanitarios de formas diferentes, pero interconectadas. sections.title: Componentes de la implementación

summary.text: Describes the four core components of digital health implementations in the Spanish edition of WHO's guideline on digital interventions for health system strengthening: accurate health content aligned with recommended practice, the digital health intervention itself, the digital applications that deliver it, and the ICT and enabling environment. A figure shows how these components fit together with governance, legislation, workforce, standards and infrastructure.

sections.extract: Las implementaciones de salud digital dependen de diversos factores, y su éxito suele estar mediado por cuestiones intrínsecas al diseño de la implementación, así como por factores externos relacionados con el entorno propicio y las TIC. La implementación de las intervenciones de salud digital se basa, en general, en estos componentes cruciales: i. información y contenido sanitario adecuados y precisos, que se

sections.title: Consideraciones globales sobre la implementación

summary.text: Stresses that digital health implementations must be adapted to local needs, users and the wider ecosystem, pointing to the WHO/ITU National eHealth strategy toolkit for assessing readiness and tabulating its enabling-environment components. It sets out practical considerations under headings such as leadership and governance, strategy and investment, legislation and compliance (privacy, consent, data security), standards and interoperability, infrastructure, workforce and health content. It closes with human rights, equity and gender considerations, including keeping non-digital services for those excluded, and the Principles for Digital Development.

sections.extract: implementación Las implementaciones deben adaptarse de forma adecuada a las necesidades locales, los usuarios previstos y el ecosistema global, compuesto por el entorno propicio y las TIC. sections.title: Investigaciones futuras

summary.text: Introduces the chapter on future research, which covers cross-cutting evidence gaps on effectiveness, resource use and human rights, equity and gender, as well as research questions specific to each intervention.

sections.extract: En este capítulo sobre las investigaciones futuras, se destacan las brechas de evidencia transversal observadas entre diversas intervenciones con respecto a la eficacia, el uso de recursos y la relación costoeficacia, y los derechos humanos, de equidad y de género. Además, se presentan preguntas de investigación específicas para cada una de las intervenciones basadas en las brechas identificadas a través del marco

sections.title: Brechas generales de la investigación

summary.text: Sets out general research gaps in digital health where evidence was of low or very low certainty, often due to poor reporting, small studies and limited settings. It calls for studies measuring both health system process improvements and distal health outcomes while tracking technical performance and user engagement, along with longer-term costing and cost-effectiveness research. It also highlights the need to study effects on equity and inequalities and implementation research on combinations of interventions, fidelity at scale and frameworks such as RE-AIM.

sections.extract: Brechas generales de la investigación En las siguientes secciones, se describen las prioridades generales de la investigación identificadas a través del proceso de esta directriz. Estas reflejan las áreas generales en las que se halló que la certeza o calidad de la evidencia eran bajas o muy bajas, o en las que no se identificó una evidencia directa. sections.title: Consideraciones para el diseño de futuras evaluaciones

summary.text: Lists issues for designing future evaluations of digital health interventions, such as using alternative designs like stepped-wedge or interrupted time-series studies for complex system-level interventions and measuring intermediate outcomes. It also notes that software changes during evaluation call for parallel process evaluations and shared tools and metrics for effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.

summary.text: Describes how WHO will disseminate the digital health guideline in full and condensed forms through regional offices and networks such as AeHIN, the Global Digital Health Network and the Health Data Collaborative, as well as consultations and webinars. It also mentions a companion planning and costing guide to help ministries implement the recommended interventions.

sections.title: Actualizaciones y enfoque de directrices activas

summary.text: Explains that the guideline will follow a living-guideline approach, with new evidence reviewed by the guideline development group and a first update adding targeted client communication for noncommunicable diseases in version 1.1. It anticipates a major update within 18–24 months and continued work with WHO's Guidelines Review Committee.

summary.text: Annex 5, presenting evidence maps that show mostly low or very low quality evidence for the effectiveness of the digital interventions reviewed, with tables by intervention and outcome type for clients, health workers and health systems. It also tabulates specific research gaps and illustrative research questions, such as the costs and cost-effectiveness of mobile learning. It notes that resource use and cost-effectiveness are cross-cutting gaps for all interventions, and ends with WHO's Geneva address.
